questions.statement: Which form of the verb "to be" is used for the plural subjects "We", "You", and "They" in the past?
questions.context: Identifying the correct past form of "to be".

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Was" is for singular subjects like I, He, She, and It.
Correct! "Were" is the past plural form of "to be".
Incorrect. "Am" is a present form.
Incorrect. "Is" is a present form.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the correct past conjugation of the verb "to be" for plural pronouns.

questions.statement: What is the negative contraction of "was not"?
questions.context: Talking about a negative past state.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Weren't" is the contraction of "were not".
Correct! "Wasn't" is the short form of "was not".
Incorrect. "Don't" is used for the Present Simple.
Incorrect. "Isn't" is used for the Present Simple.

questions.explanation:
The student remembers the correct negative contraction for the third person singular in the past.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "Yesterday, Sofia ________ at the school library in the afternoon."
questions.context: Describing where someone was yesterday in Bogotá.

options.feedback: Correct! "Was" is used for the singular subject Sofia (she).
Incorrect. "Were" is for plural subjects.
Incorrect. "Is" is present tense, and the sentence mentions "Yesterday".
Incorrect. This is the base form, not the conjugated past form.

questions.explanation:
The student understands that a past time marker (Yesterday) requires a past form of "to be" corresponding to a singular subject.

questions.statement: Choose the correct question to ask about your friends' presence at a party.
questions.context: Asking a question about a past party.

options.text: Was your friends at the party?
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Friends" is plural, so it needs "Were".

options.text: Were your friends at the party?
options.feedback: Correct! "Were" is the auxiliary for plural subjects in past questions.

options.text: Your friends were at the party?
options.feedback: Incorrect. The auxiliary must come before the subject in a formal question.

options.text: Do your friends were at the party?
options.feedback: Incorrect. We don't use "do" with the verb "to be".

questions.explanation:
The student understands the inversion of subject and verb "to be" required for past tense questions.

questions.statement: "We won the match! We ________ so happy and excited last night."
questions.context: Describing past emotions after a soccer match in Medellín.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "We" is plural and requires "were".
Correct! "Were" is the past plural form for "We".
Incorrect. "Are" is present, but the context is "last night".
Incorrect. The context (winning) implies they WERE happy, not that they weren't.

questions.explanation:
The student applies the correct past conjugation of "to be" based on a plural subject and a positive context.

questions.statement: According to the text, how was the weather?
questions.context:
A text about a past trip to Cartagena.
"My family and I were in Cartagena last week. The weather was very hot, but the beaches were beautiful. It was a great vacation."

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Weather" is singular and requires "was".
Correct! The text explicitly says "The weather was very hot".
Incorrect. The text says it was hot.
Incorrect. "They" is for plural; weather is singular.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to identify a specific past description in a text.

options.feedback: Correct! In English, we use "was born" with the subject "I".
Incorrect. Birth is a past event, so we use the past tense.
Incorrect. "Were" is not used with "I".
Incorrect. We don't use "did" with the expression "born".

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence that compares the past and the present.

options.text: Last year I was 11, now I were 12.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Now" requires the present "am".

options.text: Last year I am 11, now I was 12.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The tenses are reversed.

options.text: Last year I was 11, now I am 12.
options.feedback: Correct! "Was" for the past and "am" for the present.

options.text: Last year I were 11, now I am 12.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Were" is not used with "I".

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the temporal markers (last year, now) to select the correct verb tenses.

questions.statement: What can we analyze about the grandfather's childhood?
questions.context:
Analyzing a person's childhood description.
"When my grandfather was a child, there were no cell phones. He was very active and his favorite place was the park near his house."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says he was "very active".

options.text: Technology was different in his time.
options.feedback: Correct! The text says there were no cell phones.

options.text: There were many cell phones in the past.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says there were NONE.
Incorrect. His favorite place was the park.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes a text about the past to identify a logical deduction or fact.

questions.statement: Which of the following evaluations best describes the text?
questions.context:
A summary of a historical figure.
"Gabriel García Márquez was a famous Colombian writer. He was born in Aracataca. His books were very popular all over the world. He was a Nobel Prize winner."

options.text: It is a text about a person who is currently writing popular books.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The use of "was" indicates he is a historical figure.

options.text: It is a text about a writer who was only famous in Aracataca.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It says his books were popular "all over the world".

options.text: It is a biographical summary of a successful and globally recognized historical figure.
options.feedback: Correct! The past tense and the mention of the Nobel Prize and world popularity support this.

options.text: It is a text about why García Márquez was not a good writer.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text lists his successes.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the use of the past tense and the provided facts to identify the most accurate summary of the text.
